rv.q: It’s a magnificent piece of acting that makes you almost nostalgic for a vanished gestural style.
Altogether this is a highly recommended foray into a murky, neglected chapter of our theatrical and national history.
Adrian Lester gives an eye-wateringly good performance as Aldridge, full of peppy vigour when he arrives in Covent Garden, ready for the future.

cn.t: Adrian Lester delivers a grandeur performance in this well-received revival of Chakrabarti's play about pioneering black actor Ira Aldridge, which offers pertinent commentary on racial prejudice in 19th-century theatre.
